subject: Traffic shape and SLO alignment — post-call recap
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Grant <alex.grant@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Traffic shape and SLO alignment — post-call recap

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can size a pilot and validate SLO alignment. I pasted the raw notes below and attached a one-page worksheet for the traffic numbers you promised to share.

Key points we heard today:
- Target latency objective: p95 end-to-end response (first-byte for streaming + completion) around 450ms. You said anything >700ms is causing client retries.
- Workload mix: approx 70% short chat queries (avg 80 tokens prompt, 200 tokens response), 30% long-form generation (avg 1.2k tokens response) and about ~15% of sessions require streaming token-by-token delivery.
- Concurrency: steady concurrent sessions ~20, expected predictable peaks during business hours up to ~140 concurrent sessions for short windows (3–8 minutes).
- QPS / tokens: baseline QPS estimate TBD from your logs; we asked for a 24-hour sample and a separate 7-day peak window. For planning we flagged two useful knobs: sustained QPS and 3-minute peak QPS.
- Streaming behavior: when streaming, you observed token emission rates in the 300–500 tokens/sec range per session for long-form workflows.

Asks / next steps from Redwood:
1) Please upload the 24h sample and a representative 3–8 minute peak CSV (we've included lumen-postcall-worksheet.xlsx to capture fields we need: timestamp, request_id, model, prompt_tokens, output_tokens, latency_ms, client_region).
2) Confirm target SLOs we should model for pilot: p50/p95/p99 for both first-byte and final-complete for streaming sessions and for non-streaming requests.
3) Let us know any hard constraints (e.g., regional routing to us-east, data retention/PII rules).
4) We'll propose a two-week pilot plan (canary + controlled peak replay) and an estimated Dedicated configuration and burst policy.

Quick internal notes for Marissa / Rishi: model selection will hinge on the long-form token rates; if their long-form traffic is 1.2k tokens and they run ~30% long-form, recommend considering medium-quantized variants with aggressive KV caching. I'll draft a pilot config after Alex sends sample data.

Thanks — Soojin

Attachments: lumen-postcall-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@lumenhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 12:48:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Traffic shape and SLO alignment — post-call recap

Thanks, Soojin — appreciate the clear list. Attaching the two files we discussed (24h sample and a 7-day peak excerpt). Quick answers inline below.

Inline: 
- Baseline QPS: ~12 req/s averaged over 24h (non-uniform, see CSV).
- Short vs long split: earlier estimate holds (70/30).
- Avg tokens (responses): short ~200 tokens, long ~1200 tokens.
- Streaming sessions: when a session streams, token emission observed roughly 350 tokens/sec on average (peaks up to ~520 tokens/sec).
- Concurrency: steady ~20, business-hour crest up to 150 concurrent sessions (we see these for ~4–6 minutes when a nightly batch finishes).
- Region: all production traffic originates from us-east; we need all data processed & stored in us-east for compliance.

Constraints: SOC-type evidence is required for production; our InfoSec will want a SOC2 report + network diagram before pilot goes to prod.

I'll have my platform engineer send the raw CSVs; attached: lumen-sample-traffic-202803.csv (sample). Happy to sync on the pilot plan once you propose it.

— Alex

Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Traffic shape and SLO alignment — post-call recap

Alex — got the CSV, thanks. I profiled the sample and sketched a conservative pilot-sizing suggestion below to cover the steady baseline + expected crest behavior while keeping costs predictable.

High-level pilot sizing (recommendation):
- Canary: 2 GPU nodes (burst disabled) for 48–72 hour smoke test with replay of a 3–8 minute crest window. Validate p95 and streaming first-byte.
- Pilot (2-week): start with 4 GPU nodes with autoscale policy up to 10 nodes using a 3-minute peak target. Autoscale trigger: 85% token-CPU utilization or p95 slipping past 500ms.
- Optimization levers during pilot: prefix/KV caching for repeated context (we see a lot of similar prompts), dynamic batching with low-latency bounds, and a small warm KV cache reserved for streaming sessions to avoid cold-start token stalls.

SLOs to model for pilot (proposal):
- Non-streaming: p50 < 180ms, p95 < 450ms, p99 < 900ms for full completion.
- Streaming: first-byte p95 < 120ms; steady-state token latency (per-token time to emit) p95 < 40ms.

Commercial / ops asks:
- Marissa — can you prepare a short commercial pilot addendum (2 weeks, refundable credit) and list of evidence InfoSec will need?
- Rishi — can you draft a simple cost estimate for the 4->10 node autoscale band (assume A10-like units) and any quantization tradeoffs we should propose to the customer?

Next steps:
1) Alex: confirm you'd like the canary replay next Tuesday (21 Mar) and provide a Doc with the specific 3–8 minute crest you want replayed in the canary.
2) We'll provision the canary and send a step-by-step playbook for the replay and measurement capture.
3) We'll schedule an InfoSec pre-check (SOC2 + network diagram) with your security lead.

If that aligns, I'll get the pilot plan & RB to you by EOD Monday.

Thanks — Soojin

Attachment: redwood-pilot-plan.pdf (pilot summary stub)

From: Alex Grant <alex.grant@lumenhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Traffic shape and SLO alignment — post-call recap

Soojin — this looks good and reasonable. We want to run the canary next Tuesday (21 Mar) and will attach the 3–8 minute crest extract by EOD today to the Drive link you shared. InfoSec is fine to do an initial pre-check; I'll introduce our security lead to Marissa in a separate thread.

Small ask: can the replay tool run at a slightly accelerated wall-rate (1.25x) so we can observe queueing behavior during crest? If so, include that as an option in the playbook.

I'll also send a short PO intent note after the canary if measurements look acceptable.

Thanks — Alex
